personal_identity_summary: Margaret Brown is a 80-year-old female who has lived at the home since November 2020. She prefers to be called Margaret. Primary diagnosis is Osteoarthritis. She worked as a seamstress and values time in the garden. Staff should introduce themselves each time as she does not always retain new faces.
mobility_care_plan: Mobility status: Walking frame, supervised. Falls risk assessed as Medium. She requires supervision and prompting for all transfers. Ensure the call bell and walking aid are within reach at all times. No sensor equipment is currently required.
personal_care_plan: She requires supervision and prompting with washing and dressing and prefers to be supported in the morning. Skin integrity to be checked at every episode of personal care; pressure sore risk is Medium.
continence_care_plan: Continence needs: Continent. Toileting to be offered on a two-hourly basis and after meals. Record output on the fluid balance chart.
nutrition_hydration_plan: Diet texture: Normal. Target fluid intake 1500–2000 ml per 24 hours. Weekly weights. Fortified diet if weight loss exceeds 3 % in one month. Fluids to be offered at every interaction, not only at mealtimes.
medication_management_plan: 4 regular medicines are prescribed, administered by trained staff and signed on the MAR chart. Any refusal must be recorded with a reason and reported to the senior on duty. Covert administration is not authorised.
cognitive_support_plan: Cognitive status consistent with Osteoarthritis. Use short, single-step instructions. Avoid correcting disorientation; use validation and redirection. Familiar objects to remain in the same place in the bedroom.
emotional_wellbeing_plan: She can become anxious in the late afternoon. Reassurance, a familiar voice and time in the garden are effective. Escalate any sustained low mood to the senior carer for wellbeing review.
social_activity_plan: Enjoys newspaper reading and bingo in the lounge. Invite to group activities daily but accept refusal without pressure. Maintain contact with Pauline Brown by telephone weekly.
end_of_life_preferences: For active treatment. Advance care planning discussion held with Pauline Brown (son). Preferred place of care is the home. Spiritual needs: Church of England.
risk_summary: Falls risk Medium; pressure sore risk Medium; nutritional risk monitored monthly. Risk assessments reviewed every 60 days or after any incident, whichever is sooner.
goals_of_care: 1. Maintain current mobility with supervision and prompting and avoid unwitnessed falls. 2. Achieve the daily fluid target on at least five days per week. 3. Participate in at least three social activities per week. 4. Maintain weight within 2 kg of the current baseline.
family_involvement_plan: Pauline Brown (son) is the main contact and wishes to be informed of any fall, GP visit or change in medication. Routine update by telephone every fortnight.
